cells.tense: You are standing at the edge of a shared meaning, and the ground on both sides is solid.
cells.act: rest in the balance you already have
cells.ask: Before you walk on from this group or practice, take an evening where nothing gets decided. Let the room you are leaving and the one you are walking toward both stay as they are. Watch what settles once you stop checking.
cells.core:
The shared thing you belong to has a far edge, and you are at it able to see both sides. That is rare and hard-won — most people either cling to what is ending or leave before they have looked at it plainly. You are doing neither.

Part of you is still working the problem, checking whether you have earned the right to walk. That does not have to be solved tonight. Give the shared meaning an evening where nothing gets decided — no inventory of what the group gave you, no plan for the next one. Sit with both rooms at once. Where you are going will come into focus by itself, without being asked.
cells.sheetLine: You're at the edge and you can see both sides.
cells.place: in the shared meaning you were raised inside

cells.tense: You are already across a threshold you have not actually reached, dragging everyone with you.
cells.act: build the first new thing from what the clearing showed
cells.ask: Review the recent pushings — the moments you moved a group or tradition ahead before it was ready — and put the pattern into a line: what you reached for, and when. Then stop there. Nothing changes yet.
cells.core:
In the shared meaning you belong to, you are already at the far side. You can see what the group should become, and you are moving it there — planning the next gathering, correcting the old story, naming what has to go. The distance between where the group actually is and where you have already put it is getting wide, and you are the only one who can see it.

Next time the feeling comes, before you act on it, review the recent pushings — the moments you moved a group or tradition ahead before it was ready — and put the pattern into a line: what you reached for and when. Then stop. Seeing it clearly is the whole job for now. The next step will be yours to choose, not the momentum's.
cells.sheetLine: You've arrived somewhere the group hasn't reached yet.
cells.place: in the shared meaning you were raised inside

cells.tense: You are still standing at a door that is already behind you.
cells.act: work the pattern through to its logic
cells.ask: Take an old belonging — a group, a practice, a story you were raised in — and follow it to where it lands now. Trace the chain: what it asks of you, what it gives back, where it ends. Stop when it shows.
cells.core:
There is a door in the shared meaning you grew up inside, and it has already closed behind you. You keep standing at it — still speaking the old language, still showing up to what you left — and the group has moved on without you, or you have moved and keep the old posture anyway. Nothing is wrong with the shared thing. You are just not there anymore, and the not-being-there is the whole of where you stand.

Pushing yourself back through the door will not work. Understanding will. Take something you still carry from that tradition and follow it to its end: what it asks, what it gives, where it lands now. Do not judge it — just trace it. When the chain is clear, the next place will show itself, because you will finally be looking at where you are instead of where you were.
cells.sheetLine: You keep standing at a door that's behind you.
cells.place: in the shared meaning you were raised inside

cells.tense: You are carrying a shared meaning forward, and your account of it is that it carries itself.
cells.act: sit still until the calibration settles
cells.ask: Name one way this group or tradition works because you keep showing up for it. Sit with that for ten minutes and do nothing about it. Not to be credited — just to be counted.
cells.core:
People in this shared meaning know how to belong because you keep the shape of it — you remember the story, you hold the tone of the gathering, you make the thing feel like it has been there the whole time. If someone asked how it holds together, you would say it simply does. Your part in keeping it going has stayed off your own list.

The fatigue that is starting to show has a source. Name one way the tradition works because you keep showing up for it — one thing that would loosen if you stopped. Sit with that fact for ten minutes and do nothing about it. Not to be credited, just to be counted. The room will feel different once the one holding it knows they are holding it.
cells.sheetLine: You keep the whole thing going and don't count yourself.
cells.place: in the shared meaning you were raised inside
